findings.evidence: plot.py:64 passes fontsize=12 to the value-label text call; the module imports pyplot at line 14 and never calls plt.style.use('data-ink') or rcParams anywhere. Glyph heights measured on image-0.png: tick band rows 672-681, axis-label band rows 691-703, value label '508.26' rows 564-575.
findings.summary: The script never applies the repository's data-ink style sheet, so every label is drawn at matplotlib's defaults rather than the declared sizes, and the value labels are additionally pinned to 12 pt. Measured on the render, the x tick digits occupy 10 px of height (declared 14 pt), the axis label 'warm booking tangent [ms]' 13 px including its descenders (declared 16 pt) and the value labels 12 px (declared 14 pt). At the ~900 px reckon column that presents the page the same tick digits fall to roughly 6 px, below body text, which is the reading cost the declared sizes exist to prevent. It stays non-blocking because at the delivered 1400x720 every glyph reads without magnification and no label is clipped or lost.

findings.evidence: plot.py:17-19 define the three hex values and plot.py:51 passes them as the barh colours. Measured on image-0.png the fills render at exactly (146,146,146), (176,106,42) and (46,139,87), carrying 80520, 96990 and 79422 pixels, while each bar's identity is given by its y tick label set at plot.py:55.
findings.summary: The three bars are coloured grey, orange and green, but every bar is already named by its own row label on both panels, so the hue carries no information a reader can use; three configurations of one measurement would read better as lightness steps of a single hue, or all in one neutral. The middle hue #b06a2a renders as a muted orange-brown (RGB 176,106,42) at the dull end of the warm-brown family the plotting style retires, so beside the clean green it reads as dirt rather than as a component. It stays non-blocking: the rows are labelled, nothing is hidden and the figure is fully readable.

findings.evidence: plot.py:52 sets zorder=3 on the barh call. Measured on image-0.png, the left spine column 222 holds 260 dark pixels against 632 in the right panel's column 914; the 372-pixel difference equals the three 122-px bar bands (rows 65-186, 288-409, 511-632).
findings.summary: The bars are drawn at zorder 3, above matplotlib's default spine zorder of 2.5, so on the left panel the bars paint out their own segment of the y-axis spine and the axis line reads as three disconnected segments; the right panel's spine is continuous because its bars happen to begin one pixel to the right. The two panels therefore present the same axis two different ways in one figure. It stays non-blocking: the tick marks and labels remain, so the axis is still readable, and no data is obscured.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: pass. Two side-by-side linear panels titled by device ('H200, reserved card', 'P100 on titan'); the same three rows on both, named 'base', 'shared kernel only' and 'shared kernel + cut buckets' on one line each; every value printed at its bar end so no value has to be measured off an axis. Every glyph is legible at the delivered 1400x720 without magnification. The reading cost recorded as non-blocking finding 1 is that the type renders below the repository's declared sizes, so at the ~900 px reckon column the tick digits fall to roughly 6 px.

RUBRIC data_ink: pass. Each plot area holds three solid bars and three value labels and nothing else. Measured on image-0.png: 80520 px of grey #929292, 96990 px of orange #b06a2a and 79422 px of green #2e8b57; the largest remaining non-white colours are the raster of black text and bar-edge antialiasing. The bars carry all the visual weight.

RUBRIC decoration: pass. No gridlines (plot.py:69 sets axis.grid(False)), no background fill, no panel frame, no shadow and no styled theme; top and right spines are hidden at plot.py:67-68, so each panel draws only a left and a bottom spine. One layering default is recorded as non-blocking finding 3: the bars sit above the spine and paint out its segment.

RUBRIC contrast: pass. All text is near-black on white, far above the 4.5:1 floor, and every value label sits in white space beside its bar end rather than on a fill. The fills are graphic marks, not text: the grey reads at about 3.1:1 on white (the prescribed 'reads as data and still recedes' grey) and the orange and green at about 4.3:1, all above the 3:1 graphics floor.

RUBRIC table_form: pass. The image carries six scalars plus two device identities, but its job is the comparison a table does not give at a glance: a twenty-fold device gap on the same arm (27.85 against 580.32 ms) and one arm reversing direction between the devices (the shared kernel alone is 46 percent longer on the H200 and 2.1 percent longer on the P100, while the two cuts together are 14.4 percent longer on the H200 and 12.4 percent shorter on the P100). The exact numbers are also tabulated in the same evidence fragment, so the figure is not the only form the data take.

RUBRIC label_collision: pass. No label is clipped and none overlaps another label or the data. The render's ink bounding box is rows 15-704 and columns 18-1385 of the 1400x720 canvas, and all four canvas edge rows and columns carry zero non-white pixels. The longest row label, 'shared kernel + cut buckets', occupies columns 18-221 and so clears the left edge by 18 px; the left panel's rightmost value label and the right panel's row labels are separated by white space.
